state.title: docs(session): clarify primed_at as delivery-attempted, not consumed (#5236)
state.body:
Fixes #5236.

## What's misleading

`primed_at` is stamped when delivery was *selected and runtime start succeeded* — but several doc comments described this as "confirmed delivered" / "actually delivers," which reads as proof the agent consumed the prompt. It isn't proof of that: the issue's own qualifying incident had a worker holding `primed_at` while its trigger bead stayed open/unassigned until a manual nudge forced the claim.

## Fix — comment/doc-string only, zero behavior or schema change

- `internal/session/lifecycle_transition.go` — `PrimedAtMetadataKey`'s doc said "confirmed delivered" with no caveat; added that "confirmed" means transport succeeded, not consumption, and pointed at trigger-bead assignment as the real work-started signal.
- `cmd/gc/prompt_delivery.go` — `promptDeliveryResult`/`Delivered` docs said "actually delivered it," but `promptDelivery()` does no I/O at all (pure routing decision, per its own existing doc) — clarified `Delivered` means "a mechanism was selected."
- `cmd/gc/session_lifecycle_parallel.go` — `promptDelivered` field doc said "actually delivers the rendered startup prompt" (one of the issue's own evidence citations) — same fix.

**Deliberately left `session_level_converge.go` untouched**, even though it also uses "CONFIRMED" language for `primedAt`: that's the S19 Stage-1 migration module ("nothing reads the action list yet ... until Stage 3 wires the act loop"), and its terminology is already precisely scoped within its own durable-world/runtime-world framework — it separately tracks `primedEnv` as "delivered this runtime but may not yet be durably recorded," meaning it already distinguishes the two states this issue wants clarified. Touching an in-progress migration module's carefully-established vocabulary without Stage 3/4 context felt like the wrong call. `internal/runtime/herdr/provider.go` (the issue's other evidence citation) was already correctly worded — no change needed there either.

## Verification

`go test ./internal/session/... -run 'Primed|Priming|Prompt'` and `go test ./cmd/gc/... -run 'PromptDelivery|Primed|Priming'` both green (comment-only, no regressions); gofmt clean; `go vet` clean on changed + dependent packages; `go build ./...` clean.

state.title: bug: pool seats retired mid-claim because alias-form claims are invisible to the keep-awake and drain-ack close gates
state.body:
### Gas City version
main `ed146d8d9` (2026-09-02); the unit-level reproduction also holds on `af596339d` (2026-09-14).

### Environment
Linux (Fedora 44), tmux runtime, opencode-backed pool agents (gastown pack `gastown.polecat`, `max_active_sessions = 10`).

### Reproduction
1. Route several beads to a pool template; seats claim them with `gc hook --claim`. The claim's `assignee` is the seat alias (`GC_ALIAS`, e.g. `rig/gastown.nux`), while the session bead's `session_name` is the tmux form (`rig--gastown__nux`).
2. Let template demand drop (other beads finish) while one seat still holds an `in_progress` claim.
3. Watch the reconciler: that seat is closed with `session drained: pool slot retired by reconciler`, followed immediately by `bead.dead_assignee_reopened` for its claim, and a fresh seat re-primes from zero.

### Expected behavior
A seat holding an `in_progress` claim stays desired (`assigned-work`), is counted by `countAssignedScaleSlots`, and the drain-ack close gate sees its claim.

### Actual behavior
`sessionAssignmentIdentifierRaw`/`RawInfo` and `ComputeAwakeSet`'s `sessionAssigneeMatches` only compare `{bead id, session_name, configured named identity}`. Claims are written under the alias (`session.AssigneeIdentifier` is alias-first), so every pool seat reads as work-free and becomes a scale-down victim. The orphan-release path (`session.AssigneeIdentities`) already honours the alias, which is why the reopen follows the drain within seconds.

### Logs, screenshots, or traces
One city, 24 h, tributary pool: 122 polecat stops, 89 `bead.dead_assignee_reopened`, mean seat life ~20 min, 15–25 % of seats under 3 min; identical under three model providers, so not model-related. With the alias honoured in those three sites (see the linked PR): 22 stops and 0 reopens over the next 24 h.

### Additional context
`TestAssignmentGuardsIgnoreTransientPoolSlotAliases` states slot-form aliases (`<pool>-<n>`) must never keep a session alive. The PR keeps that guard and honours namepool aliases only. If the preferred fix is to claim under a stable identity instead (bead id / session_name), I'm happy to rework it that way.
